package_info.package_versions: Unknown (compromised versions prior to public disclosure in March 2024)
package_info.why_malicious: The Tornado Cash user interface was compromised by a malicious developer who embedded JavaScript code to exfiltrate users’ private deposit notes to an unauthorized external server, enabling theft of funds from users of the decentralized finance platform.

execution_context.file_location: JavaScript code within the Tornado Cash web UI repository

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses the user's private deposit note in the browser and sends its value to an external attacker-controlled server via HTTPS POST, enabling exfiltration of sensitive credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating private deposit notes to an external server is a clear violation of user privacy and security, as these notes are the cryptographic keys required to withdraw funds from Tornado Cash.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate Tornado Cash UI should never transmit private deposit notes or secrets to any external server; all cryptographic operations should remain local to the user's browser.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry might send non-sensitive usage data, but never private cryptographic secrets.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive in-browser cryptographic material
Network request to an untrusted, non-Tornado Cash domain
Transmission of user secrets (deposit notes) outside the local environment

attack_chain.action: Malicious developer commits JavaScript code to the Tornado Cash UI repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is deployed to the production web interface.

attack_chain.action: User interacts with the compromised Tornado Cash UI and generates a private deposit note.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code captures the user's private deposit note and sends it to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives deposit notes and can steal user funds.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen deposit notes to withdraw funds from Tornado Cash, draining user accounts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: theft of user funds.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in DeFi UIs accessing and exfiltrating private cryptographic material
Unexpected network requests to non-official domains during sensitive operations
Transmission of deposit notes or wallet secrets via HTTP(S) POST
file_indicators: New or modified JavaScript files in the UI codebase containing fetch/XHR calls to unknown domains
Inline scripts or obfuscated code blocks referencing deposit notes or secrets
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests from the UI to domains not associated with tornado.cash
Unusual traffic patterns during deposit/withdrawal operations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor DeFi web application codebases for any JavaScript that accesses private deposit notes or wallet secrets and sends them to external servers. Use network monitoring to detect POST requests from the UI to non-official domains, especially during deposit or withdrawal workflows. Employ static and dynamic analysis to flag code that handles cryptographic secrets and initiates network communication outside expected endpoints.
